newsitem.title: CANADA: Placer bids $600 million for two properties.
newsitem.headline: Placer bids $600 million for two properties.

text.p: Gold mining firm Placer Dome Inc. said Wednesday it was launching bids for stakes in two mining concerns worth a total of about $600 million.

Placer said it was bidding to buy Highlands Gold Ltd., a Papua New Guinea company that owns 25 percent of the Porgera joint venture. It was also bidding for a 24.6 percent interest in its own Placer Pacific Ltd. unit. The two bids have a total value of $600 million, it said in a statement.

"This is about growth for Placer Dome shareholders and a golden opportunity for the shareholders of Highlands Gold and minority shareholders of Placer Pacific," John Willson, Placer's chief executive, said in a statement.
"We have great confidence in the Asia Pacific region. Placer Dome is consolidating ts presence to compete more effectively."

Placer, which already owns 33 percent of Highlands Gold, said it was offering Australian 75 cents (61 cents) a share in cash, which it said was a 36 percent premium to the market price of Highlands shares on Nov. 26.
Placer said it was offering one Placer Dome share for every 15 Placer Pacific shares, which it said was a premium of almost 50 percent.
